# The Relationship Between U.S. Stock Market Returns and Treasury Bond Yields: A Statistical Analysis

This project examines the relationship between the U.S. stock market and the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield from 2000 through 2026. The S&P 500 is used to represent stock-market performance, while the 10-year Treasury yield represents conditions in the U.S. bond market. Historical S&P 500 data were obtained through Yahoo Finance, while Treasury yield data were collected from the Federal Reserve Bank of St. Louis Federal Reserve Economic Data (FRED). Using R, I analyze the relationship between daily S&P 500 returns and changes in the 10-year Treasury yield, with particular attention to how this relationship changed during the 2008–2009 Financial Crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 market shock.

```{r}
#| label: Loaded Data
#| include: false
library(quantmod)
library(fredr)
library(tidyverse)
fredr_has_key()

getSymbols(
  "^GSPC",
  src= "yahoo",
  from = "2000-01-01",
  to = "2026-08-20"
)

sp500 <- data.frame(
  date = index(GSPC), 
  sp500 = as.numeric(Cl(GSPC))
)

treasury10 <- fredr(
  series_id = "DGS10",
  observation_start = as.Date("2000-01-01")
)|>
  select(date, value)|>
  rename(treasury10 = value)


stock_bond <- sp500|>
  inner_join(treasury10, by = "date")

range(sp500$date)
range(treasury10$date)
range(stock_bond$date)

```

```{r}
#| label: Change/Return
#| include: false
library(quantmod)
library(fredr)
library(tidyverse)

stock_bond <- stock_bond |>
  arrange(date) |>
  mutate(
    sp500_return = (sp500 / lag(sp500)) - 1,
    treasury10_change = treasury10 - lag(treasury10)
  )

head(stock_bond)
```

```{r}
#| label: CleanStockBond
#| include: false
library(quantmod)
library(fredr)
library(tidyverse)

stock_bond_clean <- stock_bond |>
  drop_na(sp500_return, treasury10_change)

summary(stock_bond_clean)
```

```{r}
#| label: SP500&10TGraph
#| echo: false
library(quantmod)
library(fredr)
library(tidyverse)

ggplot(stock_bond, aes(x = date, y = sp500)) +
  geom_line() + 
  labs(
    title = "S&P 500 Perfomance, 2000-2026",
    x = "Year",
    y = "S&P 500"
  )

ggplot(stock_bond, aes(x = date, y = treasury10)) +
  geom_line() + 
  labs(
    title = "10-Year U.S. Treasury Yield, 2000-2026",
    x = "Year",
    y = "10-Year Treasury Yield(%)"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: Scatterplot
#| echo: false
library(quantmod)
library(fredr)
library(tidyverse)

ggplot(
  stock_bond_clean,
  aes(
    x = treasury10_change,
    y = sp500_return
  )
) + 
  geom_point(alpha = 0.25) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm") + 
  labs(
    title = "S&P 500 Returns vs. 10-Year Treasury Yield Changes",
    x = "Change in 10-Year Treasury Yield",
    y = "S&P 500 Daily Return"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: Line Regression
library(quantmod)
library(fredr)
library(tidyverse)

model1 <- lm(
  sp500_return ~ treasury10_change, 
  data = stock_bond_clean
)

summary(model1)
```

A linear regression of daily S&P 500 returns on daily changes in the 10-year Treasury yield from 2000–2026 found a statistically significant positive association (β = 0.060, p \< 0.001). However, the model's R² of 0.083 indicates that Treasury yield changes alone explain only a small portion of daily equity-return variation.

## How did the relationship between U.S. stock-market returns and changes in 10-year Treasury yields differ between the 2008–2009 financial crisis and the 2020 COVID-19 market shock?

```{r}
#| label: FinancialC_dataDate
#| include: false
library(quantmod)
library(fredr)
library(tidyverse)

financial_crisis <- stock_bond_clean |>
  filter(
    date >= as.Date("2008-01-01"),
    date <= as.Date("2009-12-31")
  )

range(financial_crisis$date)
```

```{r}
#| label: covid_dataDate
#| include: false
covid <- stock_bond_clean |>
  filter(
    date >= as.Date("202-01-01"),
    date <= as.Date("2020-12-31")
  )

range(covid$date)
```

```{r}
#| label: financialc_model
#| echo: false
financial_model <- lm(
  sp500_return ~ treasury10_change,
  data = financial_crisis
)

summary(financial_crisis)
```

```{r}
#| label: covid_model
#| echo: false
covid_model <- lm(
  sp500_return ~ treasury10_change,
  data = covid
)

summary(covid_model)
```

```{r}
#| label: Correlation
#| include: false
financial_crisis_clean <- financial_crisis |>
  drop_na(sp500_return, treasury10_change)

cor(
  financial_crisis_clean$sp500_return,
  financial_crisis_clean$treasury10_change
)

covid_clean <- covid |>
  drop_na(sp500_return, treasury10_change)

cor(
  covid_clean$sp500_return,
  covid_clean$treasury10_change
)
```

```{r}
#| label: Comparison
#| include: false
comparison <- data.frame(
  Period = c(
    "2000–2026",
    "2008-2009 Financial Crisis",
    "2020 COVID-19"
  ),
  
  Correlation = c(
    cor(
      stock_bond_clean$sp500_return,
      stock_bond_clean$treasury10_change
    ),
    
    cor(
      financial_crisis_clean$sp500_return,
      financial_crisis_clean$treasury10_change
    ),
    
    cor(
      covid_clean$sp500_return,
      covid_clean$treasury10_change
    )
  ),
  
  Beta = c(
    coef(model1)["treasury10_change"],
    coef(financial_model)["treasury10_change"],
    coef(covid_model)["treasury10_change"]
  ),
  
  R_squared = c(
    summary(model1)$r.squared,
    summary(financial_model)$r.squared,
    summary(covid_model)$r.squared
  )
)

comparison
```

```{r}
#| label: FinC_graph
#| echo: false
ggplot(
  financial_crisis_clean,
  aes(
    x= treasury10_change,
    y=sp500_return
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")+
  labs(
    title = "S&P500 returns vs. Treasury Yiels Changes",
    subtitle = "2009-2009 Financial Crisis",
    x = "Change in 10-Year Treasury Yield",
    y = "S&P 500 Daily Return"
  )
```

```{r}
#| label: CovidGraph
#| echo: false
ggplot(
  covid_clean,
  aes(
    x=treasury10_change,
    y=sp500_return
  )
) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4) + 
  geom_smooth(method = "lm")+
  labs(
    title = "S&P500 returns vs. Treasury Yiels Changes",
    subtitle = "Covid-19 2020 Period",
    x = "Change in 10-Year Treasury Yield",
    y = "S&P 500 Daily Return"
  )
```

The relationship between S&P 500 returns and changes in 10-year Treasury yields strengthened during periods of major financial stress. This is reflected in the increase in R² from 0.0824 during 2000–2026 to 0.1495 during the 2008–2009 Financial Crisis and 0.1405 during the 2020 COVID-19 period. Thus, changes in Treasury yields explained a greater proportion of the variation in daily S&P 500 returns during both crises.

```{r}
#| label: Crisis_stats
#| include: false
crisis_stats_long <- comparison |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(Correlation, Beta, R_squared),
    names_to = "Statistics", 
    values_to = "Value"
  )|>
  mutate(
    Value = if_else(
      Statistics == "R_squared",
      Value * 100,
      Value
    )
  )

crisis_stats_long <- crisis_stats_long |>
  mutate(
    Statistics = recode(
      Statistics,
      "Correlation" = "Correlation",
      "Beta" = "Regression Beta",
      "R_squared" = "R² (%)"
    )
  )

crisis_stats_long
```

```{r}
#| label: Stats Bar
#| echo: false
ggplot(
  crisis_stats_long,
  aes(x = Period, y = Value)
) + 
  geom_col() + 
  facet_wrap(~ Statistics, scales = "free_y") + 
  labs(
    title = "Stock-Treasury Relationship During Major Crises",
    subtitle = "Comparison of correlation, regression coefficient, and R²",
    x = "Period/Crisis",
    y = "Value"
  ) + 
  theme(
    axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 45, hjust = 1)
  )
```
